assumptions.basis: NINE-MONTH VOLUME IS NOT DISCLOSED; IT IS RECONCILED FROM REVENUE AT TWO SOURCED ASPs, NOT FROM THE MODEL'S OWN ASP. FY2025 sales were 3.51 Mt against 3.42 Mt produced [F2/F4/S8]. The company's 2026 RKAB request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and it has signed a five-year mining-services contract with PT Kalimantan Prima Persada (KPP Mining, Astra group) that lifts output from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year [S11]. Only 2 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota [F34/S6], the request for 7.8-7.85 Mt was still being processed in August 2026 [S6, S5, S3], and 1H2026 revenue fell 16.5% yoy to USD33.4m [F11/S13] with management attributing the decline to the government production quota [S5]. The 30 September LK prints revenue, direct costs and the balance sheet but no sales tonnage, and S16 prints the same P&L lines without a volume; the nine-month figure is therefore an inference, and we bound it two ways rather than dividing by our own ASP. At the FY2025 last-actual blended ASP of USD22.69/t [F2/S8], nine-month revenue of USD55.368m [F54/S17] implies 2.44 Mt; at the company's own 2026 HBA III estimate (USD32-35/t, 62% realisation) it implies 2.66 Mt [S8 p.86]. Both bounds sit ABOVE the 2.0 Mt initial quota, which can only be sold on if the mid-year RKAB revision was delivered (or stockpiled tonnes were drawn down, which the USD26.6m coal inventory [F71] permits). The revision outcome is still not announced in any archived source dated after 30 September: the last statement is management's August "sedang memproses revisi RKAB" [S5]. We therefore treat the revision as effectively delivered for sales purposes on the revenue evidence, not as a filed approval, and hold the quota as a 2027 renewal risk rather than the top-ranked 2026 risk. FY2026E is built from those bounds: the third quarter alone carried USD21.99m of revenue [F54/F11], and a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate adds about 1.05 Mt, giving 3.65 Mt — inside the 2.44-2.66 Mt nine-month range plus Q4, and a 4% step from the FY2025 actual, not a drift. We then model FY2027E 6.5 Mt and 7.0 Mt from FY2028E as the KPP ramp and the RKAB request are delivered. Holding the 2 Mt approved quota would contradict the nine-month revenue; jumping straight to 7.85 Mt would assume the filed plan is delivered in full, which is the bull case.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL, WITH THE FY2026 WAR-PREMIUM WEDGE EXPLICIT. FY2025 revenue of USD79.64m [S8] over FY2025 sales of 3.51 Mt [F2] gives a blended ASP of USD22.69/t, which is 0.209 of the FY2025A newc average of USD108.4/t and about 62% of the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t [F27/S8]. The long-run ratio is that 0.209-0.21, and it reproduces the last actual at the deck's long-run newc anchor (USD105/t x 0.21 = about USD22/t). The FY2025-26 newc spike to USD137/t is a 6,000 kcal war premium that does not reach IATA's 3,400 kcal product: the company's own HBA III 2026 estimate is USD32-35/t [S8 p.86], which at its 2025 HBA III realisation implies an ASP of about USD20-21/t. We therefore set the FY2026E newc ratio at 0.152 (USD20.8/t) and step it back toward the last-actual 0.21 as the war premium fades (0.180 in FY2027E, 0.195 in FY2028E, 0.21 from FY2029E). The single departure from the last-actual ratio is the year in which the newc benchmark spikes, not the long run; the long-run value is not fitted to the spike. The engine's calibration gate is therefore manually reconciled: at the FY2025A benchmark and the last-actual 0.209 ratio the model reproduces the FY2025 actual, while the FY2026E 0.152 is the sourced HBA III-implied wedge [S8 p.86/F27/F29].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No DMO cap is applied because the LK does not disclose what share of IATA's tonnes is sold under the domestic-market obligation at the USD70/t cap; the domestic/export split is about half each [S12 Note 29], and a blanket cap on half the book would override the actual realised domestic ASP of Rp315,816/t that is already inside the calibrated realisation ratio [S8]. The DMO cap is kept as a scenario risk in §5 instead. Sources: S12, S8.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm-per-tonne equivalent; not a physical strip ratio)
assumptions.basis: This is a pure cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio. Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads the observed cash cost per tonne; no archived source discloses IATA's bcm moved or a mine-plan strip ratio (the company reports direct costs by line only [S12 Note 30]). Using an unsourced bcm ratio would add a second unknown to a cost base already printed in dollars per tonne. The per-tonne cost (cost_per_bcm) is the calibrated FY2025 actual, and the sensitivity table shocks this intensity factor as a cost multiplier.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: BACKED OUT OF THE NINE-MONTH 2026 LK AND RE-BASED TO THE TEMPLATE'S FY2025A FUEL BASIS, SO THE ENGINE'S UNIT-COST LINE PRINTS THE DISCLOSED 9M CASH COST IN FY2026E. The nine-month 2026 LK prints direct costs of USD33.657m [F56/S17] on revenue of USD55.368m [F54]; stripping the 7.15% royalty (USD3.96m) and the depreciation inside direct costs (about USD1.93m, at 0.67/t on the implied nine-month volume of about 2.6 Mt) leaves USD27.8m of cash cost, or about USD10.64/t — the disclosed 9M per-tonne cash cost. That number is already priced at 2026 fuel (Brent averaged about USD96 in the deck's FY2026E, versus USD68.10 in FY2025A). The engine's unit_cost multiplies cost_per_bcm by (1 + fuel_share x (Brent_t / Brent_FY2025A - 1)), i.e. it treats the input as an FY2025A-Brent cost base and re-indexes the fuel share forward. Feeding 10.64 into that formula double-counts the 2026 fuel step and printed 11.56 in FY2026E — USD0.92/t (29% of FY2026E EBITDA) of pure template artefact. The input is therefore the FY2025A-Brent equivalent of the 9M cost: 10.64 / (1 + 0.21 x (96.0/68.10 - 1)) = 10.64 / 1.0860 = 9.7971, which the engine re-indexes back to USD10.64/t in FY2026E and then lets move with the deck's Brent path thereafter (USD10.28/t in FY2027E at Brent 84.0). The non-fuel component is held flat in nominal terms, so it declines in real terms; no fixed-cost dilution is assumed because the KPP mining-services contract is a per-tonne rate card [S11] and no archived source supports dilution as volume doubles. The 9M2025 comparative was USD29.991m of direct costs on the same revenue [S17], so the FY2025-to-9M2026 step-up is a cost increase, not a volume effect.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: FY2025 fuel expense of USD5.778m [S12 Note 30] over the USD27.264m cash cost ex-royalty ex-D&A gives 21.2%, so 0.21. This lets the model escalate fuel with Brent without double counting. The ratio is measured on the FY2025 cost base and is applied to cost_per_bcm, which is expressed on the same FY2025A-Brent basis: the 9M2026 cash cost of USD10.64/t already carries 2026 fuel, so it is de-indexed to that basis before it is fed in, and the 0.21 re-indexes it forward with the deck's Brent path [S17, S12].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried inside cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling, barging and port cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK [S12 Note 30/31].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regime)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 royalty of USD5.694m [F9/S12 Note 30] over FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m [S8] = 7.15%. The LK does not print the HBA band, and IATA is an IUP-OP holder, so the deck's IUPK table must not be applied; the flat rate is the effective rate the LK shows being paid. Held flat; §5 tests the upside royalty risk.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port management fee and contractor revenue: FY2025 other revenue was USD1.418m [S12 Note 29 geography table]. Held flat in nominal terms as a small non-mining line.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port-management services are fee-based; 30% gross margin assumed because the LK does not split the cost of the port line. Immaterial at about 2% of revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total fixed-asset depreciation was USD2.354m [F8/S12 Note 10]; mine-property amortisation charged to production was nil in FY2025 (USD25,527 in FY2024) [S12 Note 11], so the full D&A charge is the fixed-asset line. Over 3.51 Mt [F2] that is USD0.67/t. Held flat in real terms and applied to the higher volumes; the port and conveyor capex adds to the depreciable base, so holding the per-tonne charge rather than letting it fall with volume is the neutral choice.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: SUSTAINING ONLY; THE APE FLEET BUILD IS GROWTH AND IS EXCLUDED. FY2025 acquisition of fixed assets was USD12.565m [F42/S12 cash-flow statement and Note 10]. Note 10 splits that total between USD4.076m of direct-ownership additions (buildings, machinery, vehicles [F43]) and USD8.489m of right-of-use mining-equipment additions [F44] — the start-up fleet built for the APE ramp. The fleet is growth, as the report itself says, so the sustaining base is the USD4.076m direct-ownership portion, or USD1.16/t on 3.51 Mt of sales [F2]. The old USD2.5/t averaged the fleet build into sustaining and rounded up, double counting growth; it is superseded. The separate USD12.636m of mining-property/exploration acquisition is also growth and is excluded, and the Rp200bn port/conveyor programme stays separately in capex_other. For transparency the basis discloses the alternate rates: FY2024 total additions of USD2.659m [F47] over 3.664 Mt [F1] is 0.73/t [F45/F46], and the two-year total is 2.12/t; §4 and the sensitivity show the range. Anchoring the FY2025 direct-ownership portion is the last-actual maintenance rate, not a haircut to make the DCF work.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Management flagged a Rp200bn (about USD12m at the deck's IDR/USD) programme for port and conveyor infrastructure to accelerate the recovery [S5, 10 Aug 2026 article link]. Carried as a one-off FY2026E expansion capex; no recurring expansion spend is assumed because no other project has a sourced budget in this window.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was USD6.405m on revenue of USD79.637m, about 8.0% [S0]. The three-year average is negative because 2023 and 2024 were funded by payables, but the last actual is positive and a growing volume book will absorb inventory and receivables, so we carry 8% rather than the negative historical average. Source: S0 data pack (S0 is citable for reported financials through fin. placeholders, not for a fact entry).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: LAST ACTUAL FOR THE EXPLICIT YEARS, STATUTORY RATE AFTER. FY2025 income tax of USD1.463m on pre-tax profit of USD9.732m was 15.0% [S12 P&L]. No tax concession or binding facility is disclosed in the LK: the statutory Indonesian corporate rate is 22% [S12 Note 2n; macro deck], the FY2024 effective rate was 36.7% and the FY2023 rate 17.3%, so the 15% print is a single-year effective rate, not a permanent regime. We keep 15% for the five explicit forecast years (FY2026E-FY2030E) as the rate the LK shows being paid, then step to the 22% statutory rate for FY2031E onward. A flat 15% for thirty years would assume an unsourced permanent benefit; the step is the most likely long-run tax rate and is tested in the bear.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The rupiah bonds carry 11.25% (Series B, due Oct 2026) and 11.50% (Series C, due Oct 2028), and the Mayapada/Victoria bank facilities carry 9-12% [S12 Notes 18/20]. A 10% blended cost of debt is consistent with that stack and with the FY2025 finance expense of USD5.048m on average debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD0.227m on opening cash of USD3.298m is 6.9%; we carry 7% [S12 P&L and cash-flow statement].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new net borrowing assumed: gross debt is held at the FY2025 level. The bond Series B reached its 6 October 2026 maturity and no commitment is in the archive, so the neutral reading is a refinancing at maturity, not a repayment from cash flow; a higher coupon would lower value [S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil: the FY2025 other-income line was a net expense of USD0.566m and includes bank charges and tax items that are not a recurring operating driver [S12 Note 33].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities absorbed USD0.659m of USD8.269m net profit, 8.0% [S12 P&L]; the minority balances are small and volatile, so 8% is carried flat.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ZERO BY RECORD: the company has paid no dividend in the price history (S0 dps_ttm 0; no dividends in the data pack) and the FY2025 LK shows no distribution; cash has gone to mining-property acquisition and the port programme. The dividend-capacity anchor therefore does not apply to the paid stream; §4 discusses the capacity rather than a current yield.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed: the February-2025 rights issue took the count to 31,275.8m shares [S12 Note 27], and no further corporate action is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for USD reporting; the coal deck's long-run newc anchor is held flat in real terms [S8], so 2% is the neutral nominal allowance rather than a volume-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling expenses of USD23.206m plus operating expenses of USD5.435m, less the depreciation inside them (USD0.143m + USD0.078m), give USD28.420m of cash opex on USD79.637m of revenue = 35.7% [S12 P&L and Note 31/32]. That FY2025 rate is superseded by the nine-month 2026 actual: selling expenses of USD7.928m plus operating expenses of USD4.526m [S17] = USD12.454m on revenue of USD55.368m, about 22.5%. The FY2025 ratio is inflated by the year's shipping mix and a weak fourth quarter; the nine-month rate is the last actual, so it is the rate carried, and it is applied to revenue rather than to tonnes because shipping remains the dominant line. The red team's point that the old 35.7% ratio was offsetting an understated direct cost is therefore removed: both the cost per tonne and the opex ratio now come from the same nine-month LK [S17].

challenges.challenge: The only substantive change in the update - "the macro desk re-marked the USD/IDR spot to Rp17,509" - is an uncited, load-bearing input that the house deck's own text rejects. fund record market.fx is 17,509.1992 (asof 2026-11-05, source "Yahoo Finance IDR=X"), and the working-tree edit replaced 18,049.0 with that value. But fund record's usd_idr basis says "Spot is the reviewed onshore close Rp18,080/USD on 23-Oct-2026 (S7; corroborated S10)" and "the desk rejects the Yahoo IDR=X placeholder (17,956 asof 25-Oct, ~0.7% below the onshore close) as stale/offshore and non-citable"; the registered records are 18,080 (S7), 18,080 (S10) and 18,074 (S9), all 23 October, with no 5-6 November print. The value also breaks the deck's own forward path: FY2027E 18,350 is documented as "+1.5% vs spot", but 17,509 x 1.015 = 17,772. The rate is dispositive - at the prior model's 18,049 the target is Rp91 and the return 26.4%, i.e. BUY, not ADD - so an unsupported 3.0% strengthening of the rupiah is the entire rating action.
challenges.answer: The Rp17,509.1992 spot was the Yahoo IDR=X pack placeholder, not a reviewed print: no S# and no onshore quote, and it broke the deck own forward path (FY2027E 18,350 is documented as +1.5% on 18,080, not on 17,509). I reverted the macro deck usd_idr spot to the reviewed onshore close of 23-Oct-2026 (S7, corroborated S10; S9 printed 18,074) and recorded in the basis that no onshore print dated 3-6 Nov is archived. The target returns to Rp94.0 and the return to 30.4%, so the rating is BUY. The prior ADD was mechanically driven by an unsourced input; reverting it is stated plainly at the top of the Investment summary.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E volume anchor and the top-ranked risk cannot both be true. FY2026E 3.65 Mt is built as "about 2.6 Mt sold to September" from 9M revenue of USD55.368m [F54/S17] divided by the model's own ASP of 20.82 - a derived, not sourced, tonnage. That 2.6 Mt is already 30% above the 2.0 Mt initial 2026 quota [F34/S6] that §5 calls the highest-likelihood risk, while the RKAB revision to 7.8-7.85 Mt is described as "still being processed" in August [S5, S3]; FY2026E sales of 3.65 Mt are 83% above the only approved quota in the archive. Either the revision landed during 2026 (in which case the top risk is stale and a real bull point is omitted, and the bear's asymmetric 0.5x volume shock loses its stated justification), or the 9M tonnage is unsupported and the FY2027E 6.5 Mt ramp rests on an approval the report cannot cite.
challenges.answer: Neither S16 nor S17 prints sales tonnage, so the 2.6 Mt was circular. The nine-month volume is now bounded from revenue of USD55.368m at two sourced prices: the FY2025 last-actual ASP (2.44 Mt) and the company HBA III 2026 estimate (2.66 Mt). Both bounds sit above the 2.0 Mt initial quota, which is evidence the mid-year revision was delivered for sales; the outcome is still not announced after 30 September, the last dated statement being the August sedang memproses revisi RKAB. FY2026E stays 3.65 Mt (inside the bounds plus a run-rate Q4), the quota risk is re-ranked to a 2027 renewal risk, and the bear 0.5x volume shock is replaced by 0.8x, the company own 2025 RKAB delivery (S3). The stale USD11.4m post-BS sentence is removed.

challenges.challenge: No scenario contains the liquidity and dilution path the report itself ranks as highest-impact. At 30 September 2026, cash is USD1.45m [F58], factoring USD8.06m [F65], current liabilities USD77.35m against current assets USD62.13m [F60/F59], and the 11.25% Series B bond reached its 6 October 2026 maturity with no disclosed repayment or refinancing [S17, S12]. The base holds gross debt flat (net_borrowing 0.0) and assumes refinancing at the existing coupon; the bear only adds +200bp to cost_of_debt, and share_change is 0.0 in every scenario. §5 names a rights issue as "a second dilution path we do not model in the base case" and leaves it out of the bear as well. A USD20-30m raise at Rp45-50 adds 7-12bn shares (+22-38%), cutting value per share ~7-13% to roughly Rp77-83 and the return to 7-15% - the HOLD/ADD boundary.
challenges.answer: The bear now carries the refinancing failure as a +300bp coupon shock (Series B matured 6 Oct with no disclosed repayment, against cash USD1.45m and current liabilities USD77.35m above current assets USD62.13m), and the asymmetry is justified in qc_justifications. The rights issue cannot be a scenario switch: the engine divides per-share value by the pack share count, so a share_change shock does not flow through. It is quantified in section 5 instead: a raise at a discount adds a fifth to two-fifths to the share count and cuts value per share by a low-double-digit percentage, taking the weighted return to the HOLD boundary. The bear value is Rp10.9, essentially the discretionary-fund bridge, because the mining DCF is floored at zero equity in that combination.

challenges.challenge: The primary method prices IATA's 3,400 kcal coal off Newcastle, which the commodity card explicitly forbids ("realized price keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle"). params.price_driver is d.coal.newc with realisation 0.152 in FY2026E rising to 0.21, and the bull/bear scenarios shock d.coal.newc x1.2/x0.8 - so both the DCF value and the scenario spread are functions of a 6,000 kcal series. HBA III enters only as a prose calibration check (62.2% versus 62.1%) and as the royalty index. The model's own FY2026E newc of 137.0 is the war-premium spike the report describes, so the FY2026E ASP of 20.82 is a spiked benchmark times a ratio; no NAV on an HBA III path is shown anywhere.
challenges.answer: Accepted as a disclosure requirement, not a driver switch. The deck HBA III series is spot-only (45.53, no path, no lt) and the HBA high-GAR series is 6,322 kcal, so neither can drive a 30-year DCF; ICI-4 own basis builds its path as a fixed ratio to newc (about 0.45 in 2026E), so it inherits the same spike and its 2026 level would imply an ASP above the company HBA III estimate. Section 4 now states the anchor explicitly: the FY2025 ASP sat at the same fraction of HBA III that the FY2026E ASP takes of the company HBA III estimate, the long-run realisation returns to the last actual, and the two anchors converge within a few per cent. The newc shock is disclosed as a benchmark-year device absorbed by the realisation ratio.

challenges.challenge: The Rp91-to-Rp89 move is not reproducible from the stated single cause. Prior model fx 18,049.0 gives tp 91.01; new fx 17,509.2 gives 88.96. Pure FX pass-through is 91.01 x 17,509.2/18,049 = 88.29, but the engine prints 88.96 - Rp0.67 higher. The difference is the EV/EBITDA leg, whose peer median rose 5.200433 to 5.444985 (+4.7%) in the same run, with peer multiples moving 2.0-3.6% (AADI 4.6288 to 4.7685, +3.02%; BSSR 6.0452 to 6.2633, +3.61%), i.e. the same FX propagating through the comps. §4 says the target is lower "because the USD/IDR spot re-mark ... not because the operating case changed" and never discloses this second driver. Separately, the rupiah debt is translated at the 30 June rate: gross debt of USD57.68m, largely rupiah bonds and facilities, would be ~3% higher in USD at the new spot, another ~Rp0.97/share.
challenges.answer: The target now moves up, and section 4 discloses both drivers line by line: the FX revert (DCF leg +3.3% one-for-one, EV/EBITDA leg -4.4% because the peer median is itself a rupiah-translated multiple, net +2.2) and the scenario re-base (88.96 to 91.68 at the old FX). The rupiah-debt point is rebutted on direction: rupiah-fixed principal falls in USD when the rupiah weakens, so it does not raise net debt; the effect is a fraction of a rupiah per share and the Q3 LK seven debt lines sum within USD1m of the pack total.

challenges.challenge: The "no new information" conclusion is asserted over undated sources. S16 (emitennews) and S18 (investor.id) both carry published: null and were fetched on 5 November; S17 is the 30 September LK. The archive therefore contains no press item that can be shown to post-date 3 November, so it cannot establish that none exists - only that the file holds nothing newer. The five-session starting price is likewise inferred ("a price in the nineties ... implied by that note's expected return"), not marked: datapack price_monthly ends 2026-11 at 72 with 2026-10 at 77 and 2026-09 at 92, and there is no daily series. The report concedes the daily series is absent but still states a precise "-23% over five sessions".
challenges.answer: S18 is dated 3 Nov 2026 10:23 WIB on its own page and S16 carries 03/11/2026 11:27 WIB, so both are dated in the archive. The five-session fall is withdrawn: the pack has monthly marks only (October above the 4 November mark of 72), so section 5 now states the fall as a range between the October mark and the 4 November mark and says the daily series is absent. The no-news-since-3-November claim is restated as a gap in the file, not proof of absence.

challenges.challenge: The lead sentence asserts the opposite of the paragraph it introduces. "What changed on 6 November 2026: the tape, not the story" is followed by the report's own finding that the last mark is unchanged at 4 November, that "this adhoc is the same five-session fall", and that what changed is a macro FX input. Neither the tape nor the story changed; the translation rate did. The tone test is also unmet on the probability weight: with the bear doubled to 50% (base 30%, bull 20%) the weighted value is 0.5 x 11.38 + 0.3 x 93.52 + 0.2 x 157.42 = Rp65.2, below the Rp72 price, so the ADD depends on the 25% bear weight surviving scrutiny.
challenges.answer: The lead is retitled to what changed: an FX input we reject, not the tape or the story. The probability sensitivity is now stated in section 5: doubling the bear weight to half the distribution takes the weighted value below the price, so the BUY rests on the 25% bear weight; we hold it because the bear needs four adverse outcomes at once.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is capped below the company's own disclosed plan and below the assets the report says it cannot value. Bull volume is 1.05x (7.35 Mt) against a 7.85 Mt RKAB request [F10/S3] and a 7.8 Mt annual-report target [S8], so even the bull does not reach the filed plan; the DCF stops at 30 years leaving ~88 Mt of the 298 Mt reserve base in the ground with no terminal value, and the three non-operating IUP-OPs plus the 1,438 Mt resource [F6, S12 Note 1g] are carried at zero, contrary to the card's "development projects ... never zero". None of these appears in the bull value of Rp157.
challenges.answer: The bull volume shock is lifted to 1.12x, which takes the post-FY2026 years to the filed 7.85 Mt request (S3, S8), so the bull is the company plan rather than an arbitrary 1.05x. The three non-operating IUP-OPs and the 88 Mt reserve tail remain at zero, and section 4 now states the sourced reason: Note 1g discloses the licences and resource tonnage but no book value, sunk capex or project cash flow, so the never-zero rule has no number to enter; the bull is therefore an upper bound on the producing assets only.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 prints the nine-month cash cost per tonne as the FY2025-Brent re-based input of 9.80 USD/t (in.cost_per_bcm.FY2026E) and then, two sentences later, prints the engine unit-cost line of 10.64 USD/t and calls it "the disclosed nine-month figure, not a fuel-loaded version of it". The two sentences cannot both describe the same nine-month cost: the 9M LK leaves 10.64/t (direct costs USD33.657m [F56/S17] less the 7.15% royalty of USD3.96m less the D&A inside direct costs, over the 2.44-2.66 Mt implied volume), and 10.64 is also the figure that reconciles the paragraph own "roughly a third above the FY2025 print" (10.64 vs 7.77). The paragraph therefore contradicts itself by 8% on the number the report itself calls the single largest sensitivity in the model (QC Q1).
challenges.answer: Section 3 now prints the nine-month cash cost as fin.FY2026E.unit_cost (10.64), the engine line that reconciles the paragraph own "roughly a third above the FY2025 print", and labels in.cost_per_bcm.FY2026E (9.80) as the FY2025-Brent equivalent fed into the template so the 2026 fuel step is not priced twice. Section 4 already used unit_cost; no typed figures remain.

challenges.challenge: The summary bullet says "third-quarter gross profit was above the first half's". Q3 2026 gross profit is USD9.591m (9M USD21.711m [F55] less 1H USD12.121m [F66]) against 1H of USD12.121m: it is below the half-year total and above only the half's per-quarter run-rate. Section 3 states the comparison correctly, so the summary is stale wording. This is the sole support offered in the summary for "the operating ramp is intact", so a reader is given a false number to justify leaving volume and price unchanged (QC Q2).
challenges.answer: The summary no longer claims the third quarter beat the first half. It now states that the quarter gross profit (nine-month fact.F55 less first-half fact.F66) was below the half total but above its per-quarter run-rate, and that the ramp claim rests on the nine-month revenue and the signed KPP contract, not on a quarter-on-quarter profit gain.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says the USD2.4m exchange loss [F53] and finance costs of USD4.1m [F57] "consumed almost all of the USD21.7m gross profit" [F55]. They sum to USD6.43m, 30% of gross profit, not almost all of it; the sentence overstates the below-the-line drain by roughly a factor of three. The report's own conclusion - that the profit collapse sits below the gross-profit line - does not need the exaggeration, and a reader weighing the equity cushion is misled about how much gross profit is left (QC Q3).
challenges.answer: Section 3 no longer says the exchange loss and finance costs consumed almost all of gross profit. It now states that the two took a minority of the fact.F55 gross profit but the bulk of operating profit, keeping the point that the drain sits below the gross-profit line. No typed figures.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull caps volume at 1.05x (7.35 Mt) while the company's own 2026 request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and the annual report targets 7.8 Mt [S8], so the bull never reaches the company's plan. More important, the report's own FY2026E build implies ~2.6 Mt sold to September, above the 2.0 Mt initial quota [F34/S6], which if right means the RKAB revision has landed - a bull fact the report does not state. The stable calibration is the HBA III ratio: FY2025 ASP of USD22.69m/3.51 Mt over the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t is 62.2% [F27/S8], and the FY2026E ASP of USD20.8/t over the company's HBA III 2026 midpoint of USD33.5/t is 62.1% [S8 p.86]. The newc ratio moves only because the 6,000 kcal war premium moves (FY2025A newc 108.4 vs FY2026E 137.0), so the FY2026E 0.152 newc ratio is the same 62% HBA III realisation expressed against the spiked newc series. The FY2025 actual is reproduced at the last-actual 0.209 newc ratio; the gap is a benchmark artefact, not a cost or royalty error. [F27, F29, S8]

The residual asymmetry beyond the plan is the 2027 renewal risk, not analyst caution.

IATA is an IUP-OP holder, not IUPK [S12 Note 1g], and the LK discloses no calorific band that would let us apply the deck's IUP low/mid/high-calorie table; applying the IUPK schedule instead would be the wrong regime.

flags.message: the DCF stops after 30 years while reserves last ~82 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The 30-year cut is a value life, not a reserve life: at the 7 Mt plan the 298 Mt reserve base [F5] lasts about 42 years, but the operating IUP-OPs run only to 2028-2033 with extensions in process [S12 Note 1g]. The DCF therefore assumes the extension process succeeds for the 30-year window, stops below the full reserve life, and applies no terminal value; extending to the 93-year reserve-life arithmetic at FY2026E volume would assume successive renewals and prices that are not archived. The value of the unvalued tail is disclosed in §4 with the FY2055E remaining reserve line [F5].
